git.note: CLI built from the working tree that became 2ceb644 (rustls https + S3). The run log recorded the pre-commit parent d2e6e9a; the binary is byte-for-byte that working tree.

scope: Production HTTPS (rustls) for the remote transport, destination-pinned SSRF, an S3-compatible source, a genuine public-HTTPS acquisition of the pinned Qwen2.5-7B from Hugging Face over real TLS, atomic publication, staged Mode B inference with bit-identical parity to direct-local, and the adversarial TLS/S3/staging test suite. S3 is implemented but AWS interoperability is unverified (no real endpoint/credentials).

environment.filesystem: model + staging on ext4 (/home); repo on /mnt/e (NTFS via WSL)
environment.tls_stack: rustls 0.23.46 (ring provider) + rustls-webpki 0.103.17 + webpki-roots 0.26.11 (Mozilla root store)
environment.s3_sdk: none (S3Source delegates to the HTTP/HTTPS adapter; no aws-sdk; no custom SigV4)

https_architecture.transport: rustls TLS layered over std::net::TcpStream; one HTTP/1.1 framing + strict Range validation path for both http and https
https_architecture.certificate_validation: full chain + hostname verification via the rustls default verifier against the Mozilla root store; no insecure bypass; optional extra trusted root CA for private/custom endpoints
https_architecture.scheme_policy: public plaintext http refused by default; http allowed only under the explicit trusted-endpoint opt-in (allow_private_endpoints); https gated behind the `https` cargo feature
https_architecture.ssrf: resolve all A/AAAA; reject the host if ANY resolved address is private/loopback/link-local unless opted in; connect only to a validated resolved address (destination-pinned, IPv4 first); no re-resolution between check and connect (DNS-rebinding safe)
https_architecture.credentials: optional Authorization from LLMBRIDGE_REMOTE_AUTH, held in memory only, dropped on cross-host redirect, never logged/persisted/echoed to evidence or native FFI

public_https_acquisition.scheme: https (TLS to huggingface.co, followed the HF->CDN redirect to the object store)
public_https_acquisition.redirects: HF resolve endpoint 302 -> CDN object URL (cross-host; Authorization not carried, none used)
public_https_acquisition.wall_clock_total_including_redirect_roun: 26:14 (per /usr/bin/time; WAN, fresh TLS handshake per chunk)
public_https_acquisition.etag_note: HF's ETag differs from the file SHA-256; treated strictly as a version token, never as the content digest.

inference.common: taskset -c 0,1 llmbridge chat <model> --prompt 'The capital of France is' --max-tokens 8 --ctx 128 --threads 2 --backend streamed --metrics --sha256 <sha> --address-space-mb 2048 --workspace-mb 48 --cache-mb 32 --snapshot-reuse

https_staged_mode_b.output: Paris. It is located in the northern

direct_local_mode_b.output: Paris. It is located in the northern

inference.interpretation: Download once over HTTPS, verify once, stage locally, infer locally; decode performance equals direct-local Mode B. HTTPS is not streamed per token.

security_tests.result: 28 remote tests passed under both `remote` and `https` feature sets; 0 failed
security_tests.real_tls_accept_path: the genuine HF acquisition validated the valid-certificate + hostname + chain path against a real public CA and CDN

resource_limits.bounded_response_buffer: one chunk buffer; bounded header budget 64 KiB; no model-sized or unbounded allocation
resource_limits.connection_model: one TCP/TLS connection per range request (Connection: close); bounded retries with backoff

limitations: S3 adapter is implemented on the RemoteSource contract but AWS/real-S3 interoperability is UNVERIFIED: no AWS SigV4 signing and no cloud SDK are included, and no real S3/MinIO endpoint or credentials were exercised. S3 tests are deterministic against a local HTTP server emulating path-style GetObject + x-amz-version-id. Not claimed as demonstrated interoperability.

TLS adversarial matrix is partial: the real-CA accept path is validated by the HF acquisition and an https-against-a-non-TLS-server fail-closed test is included, but a local-CA cert matrix (expired/wrong-hostname/unknown-CA via a rustls+rcgen test server) is not yet implemented.
One TLS handshake per range request (Connection: close) makes a many-chunk WAN transfer slow (26 min for 4.68 GB here); connection reuse / coalesced-pipelined ranges are future throughput work.
WSL2, not bare metal; no IPv6 route (IPv4-first connect was required).
Windows MSVC native path not exercised this session.
Staging requires the whole model to fit on the staging filesystem; no remote computation and not unbounded model-size support.
classification: COMPLETE (evidence-backed) for: rustls HTTPS transport with chain+hostname verification, destination-pinned SSRF, default-reject of public plaintext HTTP, credential isolation, strict HTTP Range validation preserved, GENUINE public HTTPS acquisition of the pinned 7B with exact size+SHA-256 match and atomic publication, staged Mode B inference with bit-identical parity, resumable fail-closed staging, adversarial transport/TLS/S3/staging tests, and regressions. PARTIALLY COMPLETE / DEFERRED: real AWS S3 interoperability (implemented, interop-unverified) and the local-CA TLS cert matrix; Windows native untested.
